subject: Rotational reserve schedule and deal mitigations
messages:
From: Aaron Cho <aaron@bridgefall.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bridgefall Procurement <procurement@bridgefall.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity request for Q1 rollout - urgent

Marcus / Lauren —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Bridgefall is accelerating a paid pilot to a production Q1 rollout for our generative search model. Our internal ops forecast shows token volumes peaking at 6x the pilot baseline for sustained windows (8–10 hours/day) for the first 8 weeks post-launch.

Quick ask: can Redwood commit to an interim reserved capacity plan (N GPUs) or a contractual burst window that ensures tail latency stays under 350ms for our heavy routes? We need an answer to lock our calendar for launch next month.

Attached is the revised capacity profile and a short SOW excerpt. Procurement is cc'd — they will need pricing and a simple addendum if we can agree on a phased approach.

Appreciate quick guidance on tradeoffs (reserved vs. rotational reserve vs. burst).

—Aaron
Aaron Cho
CTO, Bridgefall AI
aaron@bridgefall.ai
Bridgefall AI

Attachments: bridgefall_capacity_request_v2.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Cho <aaron@bridgefall.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request for Q1 rollout - urgent

Aaron —

Thanks — read the attachment. We can’t immediately expand committed slabs without approval, but we can propose a rotational reserve schedule that gives Bridgefall a stable effective capacity while protecting other high-commit customers. High level:

- Phase 1 (first 4 weeks): schedule a nightly 10-hour heavy-window reserve (hold/rotate GPUs dedicated to Bridgefall during peak US hours).
- Phase 2 (weeks 5–8): transition to a shared reserve with guaranteed KV-cache residency for Bridgefall prefixes and a 20% burst pool for emergencies.
- Fallback: if utilization spikes >2.5x projected, automatic fallback to a lower-cost throttled variant (quantized model) for non-critical routes.

I'll attach a quick matrix with slots and rotation cadence. Need Ops (Ben) to confirm feasibility and Lauren to weigh in on pricing/contract wording. If we can agree on schedule + short addendum, legal can turn around the change order quickly.

Would you be open to a signed 8-week addendum (discounted burst + rotational reserve) rather than a multi-month commit? That gets you predictability without us over-allocating for the long term.

Marcus Lin
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rotational_reserve_matrix.xlsx, proposal_brief.txt

Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron@bridgefall.ai>, Bridgefall Procurement <procurement@bridgefall.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request for Q1 rollout - urgent

Marcus / Ben —

Agree with the phased approach. A couple of operational notes and a pricing preference from the sales side:

- Operational: rotating physical GPUs requires explicit roster coordination to avoid cache-warm penalty. Recommend reserving continuous KV-cache residency for Bridgefall prefixes during the 10-hour peak window (even if instances rotate beneath the hood). That preserves tail latency.
- Pricing: offer an 8-week addendum with a fixed daily minimum for the peak window + a capped burst budget. This is easier for procurement to sign than an open burst rate.
- Risk: if Bridgefall's sustained utilization exceeds the 6x estimate, we should have a structured escalation (automated throttling thresholds and an options ladder).

Ben — can you validate whether the roster plan (rotational_reserve_matrix.xlsx) imposes any manual runbook steps? If Ops can automate the roster, that reduces margin of error.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Dedicated & Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron@bridgefall.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request for Q1 rollout - urgent

Team —

Checked the matrix and the platform constraints. Summary:

- Feasible with automation: we can implement the rotational reserve without interrupting other customers if we enforce strict slot boundaries and pre-warm KV caches. Automation work estimated: 18–24 hours of engineer time + 2 scheduled runs to validate.
- Roster approach: prefer 3-day rotation blocks (swap a subset of reserved GPUs every 72 hours) to minimize cache churn while preserving fairness.
- Contention policy: recommend a laddered entitlement: 50% guaranteed during peak window, 30% reserve (rotational), 20% burst (pre-approved). If Bridgefall exceeds 85% of the ladder for 2 consecutive days, trigger an Ops review and pricing re-evaluation.

I attached a one-page ops plan (gpu_roster_plan.pdf). If we automate the roster, manual intervention should be minimal. Also note: legal will want the burst definitions precise — define "burst" in tokens/min and cost cap.

Ben Carter
Capacity Ops Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Cho <aaron@bridgefall.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Bridgefall Procurement <procurement@bridgefall.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request for Q1 rollout - urgent

Marcus / Lauren / Ben —

Appreciate the thoughtful options and the ops plan — this is helpful. Bridgefall is willing to sign an 8-week addendum that mirrors the laddered entitlements you proposed (50% guaranteed / 30% rotational / 20% burst) provided the following are included:

- A clear definition of "burst" including token/min thresholds and a worst-case billing cap for the period.
- An automated roster so we don’t face cache-warm latency surprises during rotation swaps.
- A 48-hour escalation SLA to confirm engineering changes if we hit the 85% threshold.

Procurement will circulate a short addendum draft once we have those three items written into the proposal. Happy to move fast.

Thanks again — looking forward to the phased rollout.

—Aaron
Aaron Cho
CTO, Bridgefall AI
